method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, forward reconstruction of the two chaining steps, the conjunction step and the quantified-rule step, plus exact formula, macro, token, label, reference-option and identifier comparison; no independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: A worked axiomatic derivation of the implication from a conjunction of two universal formulas to the universal closure of their pointwise conjunction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Give a derivation of the implication from for-all-x A and for-all-y B to for-all-x of A and B at x.
samples.checks: The antecedent conjunction, the distinct bound variables x and y, the final universal x and the pointwise conjunction remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Use ax:land1 and ax:q1 with the chain proposition to obtain the antecedent implies A(a), and use ax:land2 and ax:q1 similarly to obtain the antecedent implies B(a). An appropriate ax:land3 instance and two modus-ponens applications give the antecedent implies A(a) and B(a). Then QR universally generalizes the consequent at x.
samples.checks: Both projection branches, both ax:q1 instances, both prop:chain references, ax:land3, two MP applications and the final QR direction are preserved. The constant a does not occur in the empty premise set or in the antecedent conjunction, so the cited quantified rule's side condition is satisfied.

source_observations: The two universal assumptions use different bound-variable letters before both are instantiated at the same constant a; the Marathi leaves those letters unchanged.
The final QR application is universal generalization in the consequent of a conditional, matching the first quantified rule rather than the dual existential rule.
No formula, macro, token, label, identifier, reference option or side condition was changed.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
